findings.title: Meeting closet corner: at zoom 9 and a low orbit the camera ends up inside or behind an uncut wall, so the whole screen is beige and Pip is gone
findings.problem: At spawn by the server closet (about −11.3, −7.4) at zoom 9, 3 of the 8 yaws in a low-pitch sweep (orbit(0,−200), then −180 px steps) fill the whole 1440×900 frame with one flat beige wall face. Pip, the plug, the reel and the job are all invisible. Only the HUD is left, still saying 'F Pick up the plug'. The same happens at yaw steps 375, 625 and 750 in the first sweep. At the default pitch one yaw (def-3) also hides Pip behind the closet wall cap and the server racks. The same sweep in the Lunch corner (14.5, 8.4) never blanks: the walls cut away correctly there. So this is room-specific, not general. The cause is probably the cutaway test in src/game.ts:383-385. It decides per wall, using the wall group's centre (`wall.group.parent.getWorldPosition`) and `normal·toCam > .2`. When the camera sits past a corner, the vector from the centre of a long back or left wall to the camera is nearly parallel to the wall, the dot falls below 0.2, and the wall stays 3 m tall between the camera and Pip. Nothing pulls the camera in when it is inside a wall. This is the room where the player spends the first 20 s, and the corner is the spawn point. Right-dragging there is exactly what a new player does to 'look around', and the screen goes blank. This is not the known 'stub hides Pip's legs' finding from the Playground. Here the whole frame is lost.
findings.fix:
In src/game.ts updateCamera:
(1) Run the cutaway test from the nearest point on each wall segment to the camera, not from the wall centre. Or use `normal·toCam > 0` together with 'the camera is on the outside half-space of the wall plane': `(cam - wallPoint)·normal > 0`.
(2) Add a camera pull-in. Raycast from the focus to the wanted camera position against the shell walls and the interior walls (or the static colliders), and clamp the distance to hit − 0.3 m.
(3) As a safety net, if the frame is filled by one non-occluder, raise the pitch to at least 0.55.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/recheck-list/corner.mjs (meeting at −11.3, −7.4; zoom 9; 8 yaws at default and low pitch). Every frame should show Pip, with a luma std > 30 in the centre region (today's failures measure 25–34 with a flat frame). Add a playwright check that no orbit at the spawn returns a frame whose centre 400×400 crop is a single colour.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced this. In Meeting I walked to (-11.3,-7.4), zoomed to 9, orbited (0,-200), then swept 8 yaws in -180 px steps. Frame 4 is one flat beige wall: the centre 400×400 crop has a luma std of 1.3, against 37–62 for the other frames. In frame 3 Pip is completely hidden behind the closet wall cap and the dark racks. In frame 7 he is mostly hidden behind clutter boxes. The geometry backs up the stated cause. shellWall (src/levels/decor.ts:32-40) is the full-length back wall (z=-10, centre x=0) and side wall (x=-16.5, centre z=0). The cutaway at src/game.ts:383-384 uses the centre of the wall group. With Pip in the far-left corner, a camera 8.6 m out behind the side wall (about x=-18, z=-15) gives toCam from (-16.5,0) of about (-0.1,-1). Its dot with the normal (-1,0) is about 0.1, below the 0.2 threshold, so the 3 m wall stays up between the camera and Pip. Nothing pulls the camera in (src/game.ts:381-382). One caveat: the Lunch control proves little. (14.5,8.4) is the front-right corner, and that corner has no shell walls (decorate builds only back and side, src/levels/decor.ts:73), so it could never blank. It isn't P0, because one more drag recovers the view. The fix is sound. Option (1), the half-space test of the camera against each wall plane, is the minimal correct change. The pull-in raycast in (2) must ignore the interior walls, which already fade, or it will fight the fade.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap3-recheck-list-08-closet-contact.jpg (my 8-yaw contact sheet; frame 4 blank, frame 3 Pip hidden)
src/levels/decor.ts:73 (only back and side shell walls exist, so the Lunch front-right corner is not a valid control)
src/levels/meeting.ts:33 (width 33, depth 20: back wall z=-10, side wall x=-16.5, both centred far from the closet)
findings.fix_correction: Keep fix (1): stub when (cam - nearestPointOnWallSegment)·normal > 0, or when the camera is past the wall plane. For (2), raycast only against the shell walls' tall upper parts, not the fading interior walls (game.occluders), so the pull-in and the fade don't fight. The Lunch control should be replaced by a corner that actually has shell walls, e.g. Lunch's back-left corner.

findings.title: REGRESSION / still open LR7 + QA 5: kitchen and closet half-walls hide Pip's lower half at zoom 9 without fading
findings.problem: LR7 (kitchen/corridor wall) and QA 5 (Meeting interior walls) were marked FIXED: 'interior walls fade' (src/levels/decor.ts:44-49). At zoom 9 with Pip at about (−6.8, −0.67), just inside the kitchen, the purple store-front section fades but the teal kitchen-front-left wall in front of him stays opaque. It cuts him off at the belt. At the higher orbit (orbit(0,+200)) the orange wall cap covers him up to the shoulders, and only the hat and one shoulder show, about 25–35% of Pip. The Meeting closet wall does the same at yaw −500 (Pip visible only from the waist up), and the dark server racks are not occluders at all (yaw −750: only the hat shows). The cause: the fade uses one ray to Pip's hip (`p.y+.4`, src/game.ts:387). A 1.35 m half-wall between the camera and Pip's legs is missed whenever the ray clears the cap. DR-12 asks for at least 70% of Pip visible. The walls do fade when the ray hits, so the fix is partly there, but the player-facing complaint (the wall hides Pip) is back at close zoom.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:387, cast three rays: to Pip's feet (p.y−.6), chest (p.y+.4) and head (p.y+1.0). Fade any occluder hit by any of them. Add the Meeting server racks and the Lunch storeroom rack (decor.ts:189) to game.occluders, or move them to root with cloned transparent materials like interiorWall does. Also lower the faded opacity from .15 to at most .25 per DR-12 (it already meets that).
findings.verify: Retake recheck-list-05b/05c and 04d/04f. Pip's boots and belt must show through a translucent wall. Count Pip pixels (mask by the blue overall hue) and require at least 70% of an unoccluded reference.
findings.verify_reason: I looked at the cited shots. In recheck-list-05b the purple store wall is translucent but the teal kitchen-front wall stays opaque and cuts Pip at the belt (about 55% of him visible). In 05c only the hat and a sliver of shoulder show over the orange cap. In 04f Pip is visible from the waist up behind the near wall. The code matches the claim. src/game.ts:387 casts a single ray to (p.x, p.y+.4, p.z), about 1.17 m above the floor, and interior walls are 1.35 m tall (src/levels/decor.ts:44). From a raised camera the ray can pass over the cap while the wall still covers Pip's legs. The server racks are not in game.occluders: in my own sweep (verify-gap3-recheck-list-03) Pip is fully hidden behind the dark racks and the closet cap. The storeroom rack at src/levels/decor.ts:188-189 is drawn under decorRoot with shared toon materials, so it can't fade either. Calling this a 'regression' overstates it: the fade works when the single ray hits. It is a gap in that fix. One part of the suggested fix is muddled: the faded opacity is already .15, so 'lower to at most .25' is a no-op.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap3-recheck-list-03-meeting-closet-low.jpg (Pip fully hidden by the closet wall cap and the non-fading racks)
src/game.ts:386-388 (single ray to p.y+.4; faded opacity already .15)
src/levels/decor.ts:44-49 (interior walls h=1.35, the only things pushed to occluders)
src/levels/decor.ts:188-189 (storeroom rack on decorRoot, shared materials)
findings.fix_correction: Cast 3 rays (feet p.y-.6, chest p.y+.4, head p.y+1.0) and fade any occluder hit by any of them. Move the server racks and the storeroom rack onto game.root with cloned transparent materials and push them into game.occluders. Drop the opacity change; .15 is already below .25.

findings.title: REGRESSION (partial) L6: R on the pause card instantly reloads the job, and Tab on the result card drops focus to <body>
findings.problem:
L6 said Tab and R act only during play. Checked by key presses with a reload marker:
- Title: Tab focuses Play and R does nothing. PASS.
- Jobs board: Tab focuses Home and R does nothing. PASS.
- Result card: R does nothing. PASS.
- Pause card: R reloads the page straight back into play (window marker lost, screen 'play'). It throws the run away with no confirm. `playing=this.running&&!this.won` (src/game.ts:166) is still true while paused. The pause card prints a small 'R' keycap on Restart (shot 11c), so this may be a deliberate shortcut. It still breaks DR-22's 'No game key acts while a menu is open', and R sits next to E/F/Q. meeting-play already reported R in play. This is the menu case.
- Result card: Tab moves focus from the 'Next job' button to BODY, so a keyboard player loses the card's buttons. On the other screens Tab moves to the next button.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/recheck-list/lobby.mjs output: PAUSE afterR {screen:'play',mark:false}; RESULT afterTab focus BODY
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:166, change the R condition to `playing&&!this.paused`. If a pause-card shortcut is wanted, handle R in src/ui/game-ui.ts as a click on [data-ui=restart] with a hold-to-confirm or a second press, and keep the keycap. On the result card, don't let the canvas keydown preventDefault-skip focus: either leave Tab to the browser while won (it already is) and make the card's buttons tabbable, or trap focus inside `.screen[data-screen=result]`.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/recheck-list/lobby.mjs. PAUSE afterR should keep mark:true and screen 'pause'. RESULT afterTab focus should be 'jobs-reload' or 'restart', not BODY.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the behaviour, but it is not the bug described. (a) R on the pause card is a deliberate, labelled shortcut. The pause card's Restart button carries a visible 'R' keycap (src/ui/screens.ts:156). src/ui/game-ui.ts:119 explicitly sets flagAutostart for R when the screen is 'pause' so that the reload goes straight back into play. A menu button's own labelled shortcut is not a 'game key acting while a menu is open' under DR-22. My run: pause → R → screen 'play', mark false, as designed. (b) Tab on the result card wraps normally: from Next job (the last button) it goes to BODY, then restart → jobs-reload → nextjob. That is ordinary document tab order; the buttons are not lost (all have tabIndex 0). The real problem is the inverse. The result card's Play-again button also shows an 'R' keycap (src/ui/screens.ts:198, visible in my shot 10), but R does nothing there. src/game.ts:166 requires !this.won, and game-ui.ts:119 only sets the autostart flag without restarting. A keycap that does nothing is the actual inconsistency.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap3-recheck-list/result.mjs output: result start focus nextjob → Tab BODY → restart → jobs-reload → nextjob; afterR screen 'result' mark true (R dead); pause afterR screen 'play' mark false
src/ui/screens.ts:156,198,225 (R keycaps on pause, result and fail restart buttons)
findings.fix_correction: Leave R on pause alone, since it is labelled. Either make R on the result card call the restart action (in src/ui/game-ui.ts key(): if s==='result'||s==='fail' and KeyR then this.restart()), or remove the 'R' keycap at src/ui/screens.ts:198. Tab needs no change.

findings.title: Lunch: 'F Plug into the capacitor cart' seats the plug and a cleaner bot rips it out the same frame, with no readable cause
findings.problem: The run was: Supply A thin cable walked straight to the docked capacitor cart (via (.3,2.4) and (10,1)), with no cable bridges laid. The prompt reads 'F Plug into the capacitor cart' (shot 09f). The plug connects (lunch.interact returns true, ports ['a','cap']) and on the next step ports is back to ['a',null]. Strain is only 0.876 after seating, so the 1.25 yank rule isn't the cause. The bot-snag rule (src/lunch-runtime.ts:259-260) is. A bot on its loop was already over the freshly placed segment, so the snag fired on frame 1. To the player, F 'does nothing': the cable just drops at their feet. The spark burst is near the bot, not at the cart, and the prompt flips to 'E'. They never learn that the cable crossed the bots' line. Laying the two bridges first (as tests/lunch.spec.ts does) makes the same plug work (charge 12 → 6.9 at the kick, then it recharges). So the rule works, but the failure doesn't explain itself, which breaks DR-28 and DR-37.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/recheck-list/lunch-b.mjs (earlier variant log: DIRECT r:true ports ['a','cap'] → next step ['a',null], strainAfter .876)
findings.fix:
In src/lunch-runtime.ts:
- Don't let a bot snag a cable in the first 1.5 s after it was plugged. Instead, have the bot visibly bump into it and stop, then snag after a 1 s wobble with the cable end flashing.
- Put the spark and alarm at the unplugged end (cable.ends[end]), not only at the bot.
- When the held cable's preview path crosses the LANE and there is no bridge, show the prompt 'F Plug in (the bots will snag it)', or tint the crossing segment red while holding.
findings.verify: Script: from A, carry thin-1 to the cart without bridges and press F. Expect the plug to hold for at least 1 s, a visible bot bump at the crossing, and a spark at the unplugged end in the screenshot. With bridges, ports stays ['a','cap'] (as today).
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the direct, no-bridge plug of thin-1 from Supply A to the docked cart via (.3,2.4) and (10,1). It did NOT snag on the same frame. Ports stayed ['a','cap'] for about 2.5 s, until the bot on the x=-1 edge of the lane reached the crossing. At that point the plug end was dragged along with the bot for 4 s, which is visible in verify-gap3-recheck-list-23: the cable runs to the bot near the kitchen. So the cause can be seen; the bot visibly drags the plug. The real clarity problem is distance. The snag happens about 12 m from the cart, and the spark and alarm sit at the bot (src/lunch-runtime.ts:260). At the cart, Pip just sees the cable vanish (shot 22). The 'same frame / drops at the feet' version depends on timing and I did not reproduce it. The snag rule has no grace period (src/lunch-runtime.ts:259-260), so a frame-1 snag is possible when a bot is already on the segment. Since this is the chaos path (bridges are the intended solution) and the rule is readable when on screen, P2 rather than P1.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap3-recheck-list/lunch.mjs log: plugged at t=44.87 ['a','cap']; held until t≈47.37 when bot0 at (-1,1.71) snagged; end1 dragged to (1.1,1.2) by t=50.67
mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap3-recheck-list-22-lunch-direct-snag-plus1s.jpg (at the cart: cable gone, no local cue)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap3-recheck-list-23-lunch-direct-snag-zoomout.jpg (bot dragging the plug end at the lane edge)
findings.fix_correction: A plug-in grace period isn't needed. The bot already shows the cause by dragging the plug for 4 s. Add a cue where the player is: a spark and dust burst at the old port position (the cart inlet) when the snag fires, and alarm the old port as well as the bot position. Optionally tint the held cable's lane-crossing segment while it is carried and no bridge is near.

findings.title: Cable cut by the swing door is called 'burned' in the repair prompt
findings.problem: When the unwedged door slams on the thick cable, the cable dies at the door (red bolt over the door, shot 07a). Walking to it, the prompt reads 'F Repair the burned cable (costs 15)'. The same string is used for every dead cable (src/lunch-runtime.ts:195), whether it was scorched by overload, cut by the door or snagged. This room teaches 'cable rating and heat' as a separate idea, so calling a mechanical cut 'burned' muddles cause and effect (DR-28 says the sentence names the physical cause; DR-34 asks for physically right wording).
findings.fix: Record the death cause on the lead (e.g. `lead.cause='cut'|'scorch'`) where it is set (door cut at :248, scorch in the sim). Then prompt 'F Repair the cut cable (costs 15)' or 'F Replace the scorched cable (costs 15)'.
findings.verify: Run the 'swinging door cuts a cable' path (tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts:24) and check that .prompt-pill contains 'cut'. Run the thin-cable overload path (:16) and check that it contains 'scorched'.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches the claim. The door cut at src/lunch-runtime.ts:248 sets cable.lead.dead=true, and the prompt at :195 always reads 'Repair the burned cable (costs 15)' for any dead lead. Screenshot recheck-list-07a shows the red bolt over the swing door with the pill 'F Repair the burned cable (costs 15)'. A mechanical cut is called 'burned' in a room that teaches heat and rating separately (DR-28/DR-34).
extra_evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:248 (door cut sets dead with no cause)

findings.title: Inline capacitor docking works but its lead to the winch is unreadable at the game camera
findings.problem: LR9 is functionally fixed: the cart docks within 2 m (capDocked true), thin-1 plugs into the cart, and the lift starts with atLoad true and the charge drawn 12 → 6.9. But the only visual sign that the cart sits *between* the supply and the winch is capCord: a thin #3a3d55 dark tube (src/lunch-runtime.ts:56, :324-325). At zoom 9 it is a short black curve over the cart. At the game camera it can't be seen, and the plug end sits at y 1.22 at Pip's hand, so he looks like he's still holding it. DR-37 asks that invisible wiring be drawn, and LR13's 'can players see it?' remains a no.
findings.fix: Draw capCord in the same cable material and radius as the thin leads (cream #ece8dc, r≈.06) with a yellow job-plug at the winch socket. Lower the cap port to y≈.6 so the plugged end rests on the cart's inlet, not at hand height. Give the cart a small charge gauge (needle or 3 bars) that drops at the kick and refills, so 'it supplies the kick' reads without text.
findings.verify: Retake recheck-list-09d at the game camera. The cart→winch lead and the gauge dip at the lift start should be visible in a 300×300 crop.
findings.verify_reason: capCord is a TubeGeometry of radius .05 in dark #3a3d55 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:56, :325) that runs from the cap port to (12.62,.38,-4.8) under the cart. In recheck-list-09e (zoom 9, lift running) no cart→winch lead can be seen. The thin cream cable ends in a white plug raised at Pip's hand height. My log shows the seated end at y=1.22 (cable end1 {x:11.6,y:1.22,z:-5.33}), so Pip looks like he's still holding it. The cap port is created with a .75 height offset on the cart (src/lunch-runtime.ts:54). The capacitor's role is not drawn (DR-37).
extra_evidence: verify-gap3-recheck-list/lunch.mjs log: thin-1 end1 y=1.2248 while ports ['a','cap']

findings.title: Books use job yellow #ffc94d, so every bookshelf carries job-coloured blocks
findings.problem: This turned up while re-checking the bookshelf colour wrap (which passes: every row is filled in both rooms). The book palette at src/props/prefabs.ts:52 includes '#ffc94d', the exact job-item yellow from DR-45. Every shelf in the Meeting lounge and around the Playground lamp shows 5–6 job-yellow blocks at chest height, next to the job's own yellow plug and reel. The earlier report only called the books 'saturated candy bars'; the job-yellow collision is what breaks DR-45.
findings.fix: Replace '#ffc94d' in `books` with a desaturated ochre such as '#d9b36a', and drop the saturation of the others about 30% (DR-51: books are desaturated).
findings.verify: Retake recheck-list-01b/01d. No book pixel should be within 25 ΔE of #ffc94d.
findings.verify_reason: src/props/prefabs.ts:52 has '#ffc94d' in the books palette, and the bookshelf builder (:123-125) cycles that palette across every shelf row. DR-45 (mockups/review5/RULES.md:284) says no decorative clutter uses job yellow #ffc94d. Yellow books are visible on the Playground shelf in my result-card shot. The problem is wider than books. The same file gives job yellow #ffc94d as the default colour of the mug (:12) and the beanbag (:26), and it appears among the desk-cable colours (:45) and lamp colours (:47) and on a part at :151. The fix should cover all of these, not only the books.
findings.fix_correction: Replace '#ffc94d' in books with a desaturated ochre such as '#d9b36a' and desaturate the rest about 30%. Also re-colour the decorative non-job uses at src/props/prefabs.ts:12 (mug), :26 (beanbag), :45, :47 and :151. Keep #ffc94d for actual job items such as the reel, bridge, splitter and wedge.

notes.playability: Most re-check items hold up on real screenshots. The bigger gap I found is the camera. At the Meeting spawn corner, zoom 9 plus a low orbit puts the camera behind an uncut wall in 3 of 8 yaws, and the whole frame goes beige. The Lunch corner doesn't do this. Also, because the fade uses one ray to the hip, half-walls (kitchen front, closet) hide Pip's legs and torso at close zoom without fading. Strip snap (M10) is forgiving: dropped at 2.44 m it snapped onto the door spot with a ring burst. L5 works: Jobs from the result card goes to the lobby, and F5 lands on the title, not the Jobs board. Keys: Tab and R are inert on the title, Jobs board and result card. R on the pause card reloads the job instantly; the card advertises it, but it is still a game key acting inside a menu. All scripts closed their browsers with zero console errors.
notes.teaching: The capacitor chain (LR9) and no-recharge-while-tripped (LR10) are truthful. In the run the kick drew the cart from 12 to 6.9, it then recharged only from the live supply, and the unit test 'a capacitor recharges between lift starts only from a live supply' passes (vitest, 9/9). The cut-cable meter (LR6) no longer flashes gold: the strain card faded with no 'connected' class. The weak spots are explanation, not simulation. The bots snag a fresh plug on frame 1 with no readable cause. A door cut is called 'burned'. The cart's inline lead is a black hairline nobody will see at the game camera.
notes.clarity: The vending machine faces +z with its window and products toward the player (LR2 PASS). The Lunch swing leaves stay upright after shoving through and back; they only rotate on y (lunch-runtime.ts:227). Window shafts are no longer hard wedges; at the game camera and at zoom 9 they're barely visible at all. On the Meeting back wall the windows sit behind cabinet rows with boxes on top. The pins and spool exist (P4): six pins at their homes, a yellow spool by the anchor. The spool's remaining length is still unreadable at the game camera (already reported).
notes.fun: The title hero shot (P7) works: Pip stands in the right third beside the logo and the sparking-plug glyph. His raised arm is cropped by the right edge, a small composition miss. The Playground win sequence (confetti, Pip cheering by the lit lamp) is charming, but the result card took more than 4 s to appear in manual time.
notes.models: The bookshelf colour wrap (prefabs.ts:123-125) is fixed. All three rows have 7 coloured books in the Meeting and Playground at zoom 9, with no missing or black blocks. The palette still includes job yellow. The Lunch door leaves are solid two-part leaves with porthole windows and read well. The capacitor cart reads as 'blue cylinders on a trolley', with no gauge to show its job.
